paragraphs:
Mar son of Rav Ashi, before Rava, chapter HaMotze Tefillin 102b. This would make his father the early Rav Ashi, since Rav Ashi was born on the day Rava died. He did not see Tosafot there concerning Mar son of Rav Ashi's statement: 'I stood before Rava; my dressing fell onto a cushion, and he replaced it. I said, "Does the master not accept Rav Ḥisda's statement?" He answered, "I do not accept it."' Tosafot writes: Rabbenu Ḥananel reads 'I stood before Father' rather than 'before Rava.' This is also our Gemara's reading and Asheri's. Rif reads 'before R. Abba'—this seems wrong; examine his generation. It likewise seems one should not read 'before Rava,' since Rav Ashi was born when Rava died. End of quotation.

You thus see that Tosafot does not regard this as the early Rav Ashi's son, contrary to Yuḥasin's opinion. Necessarily that opinion is incorrect: the early Rav Ashi lived in Rav's days, as did his son Mar, since above Rav Assi visited Rav Ashi's house at Mar's wedding. Rav Ashi died immediately after Rav's death (see his entry), so the early Mar was grown when Rav died. The early Rav Ashi was Rabbi's student, saying 'Rabbi said' (see his entry). We also find R. Ḥanina saying that Rav Ashi said (see his entry); Ḥanina was known as Rabbi's student, whom Rabbi directed to sit at the head. Although Rav Ashi said in Rav's name (see his entry), he was at least grown and approximately his colleague. Rav Huna was Rav's student; Rav Ḥisda was Rav Huna's student. How could Mar ask his father whether he accepted Rav Ḥisda, a student's student, even if Rav Ashi lived in Rav Ḥisda's time? See Halikhot Olam: one does not cite a teaching from someone junior. Thus Tosafot, Ḥullin 14, wonders why Rav Huna brought proof from Rav Ḥiyya bar Rav's exposition, since he was junior to Rav Huna (see his entry and the general rules). See the early Rav Ashi; on every opinion Rav Ḥisda was junior. How could his son ask him whether he accepted Rav Ḥisda? Tosafot therefore had to interpret this Mar as the later Rav Ashi's son, reading 'before Father'; Yuḥasin erred.

Nevertheless, there must have been two Mars son of Rav Ashi: one, the early Rav Ashi's son, at whose wedding Rav Assi was present, as above. Rav Oshaya spoke to Mar son of Rav Ashi, Ḥullin 58b. The context seems to indicate the later Mar. But Rav Oshaya occurs in Rav Assi's time and before Rava, while Rav Ashi was born when Rava died; thus it is the early Mar. Mar son of Rav Ashi said, 'I disqualify myself from judging a Torah scholar, for he is as dear to me as myself,' Kol Kitvei 119a. From the context, which previously cites Rava saying, 'May I be rewarded that when a Torah scholar comes before me for judgment, I do not lay my head on a cushion until I have sought arguments in his favor,' this Mar appears to be the later one.
